chunks: Indeed, the deeds of the servants are presented to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and to the Imams عليهم السلام every day, their righteous ones and their wicked ones. So beware. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And say: Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers."

key_terms.أَعْمَالَ: deeds or actions performed by people
key_terms.الْعِبَادِ: the servants, meaning human beings accountable before Allah
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: the believers, understood here in the hadith’s context as the divinely designated believers
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the verse "And say: Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers"?
ai.summary: This report explains the verse as indicating that the deeds of people are presented regularly to Allah’s Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Imams عليهم السلام. It serves as a warning toward moral vigilance, since both righteous and sinful acts are laid open before divinely appointed witnesses.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"The deeds of the servants are presented to the Messenger of Allah (sw) and to the Imams (as) every day, both the good and the evil ones.
So beware! This is the meaning of Allah’s (swt) statement:
'And say: Work; so Allah (swt) will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers' (Surah At-Tawbah 9:105)"
